episodes.title: DETROIT'S BIZARRE CULT: DAYS OF INSULTS, DRUGS & A SNAKE IN THE MAILBOX!
episodes.description:
A cult in Detroit promised to help drug addicts get clean. The treatment? Days of screaming insults at one another. And you thought THIS podcast was dysfunctional.

Journalist Amelia Benavides-Colon returns to The Soul of Detroit to take ML Elrick, Marc Fellhauer and Shawn through the strange history of Synanon — a California-born addiction rehabilitation movement that established its only Midwest chapter right here in Detroit.

At the center of it all was something called “The Game.” It could go on for days and involved members hurling insults at one another in the name of recovery. Sounds a little like group therapy with a serious anger-management problem.

Amelia explains Synanon's connections to Alcoholics Anonymous, how the organization operated in Detroit, and how its founder, the charmingly named Chuck Dederich, eventually found himself in trouble with the law. His response? Apparently, putting a snake in a prosecutor's mailbox. Because that's how reasonable people settle disputes.

But before we get to the cult, there's plenty of other business to attend to.

ON THIS EPISODE:

Why did a drug rehabilitation organization turn into a cult?

What exactly happened during Synanon's bizarre “Game”?

How did Synanon's founder go from helping addicts to running afoul of the law?

What do Red Hot Chili Peppers frontman Anthony Kiedis, a 19-year-old girlfriend and ML's dating rules have in common?

Why did Duke students walk out on Jerry Seinfeld during his commencement speech?

Shawn explains why the relationship between college students and Ann Arbor squirrels is a barometer for civilization.

Marc gets grilled about his alleged experience with an impressive assortment of recreational drugs.

And ML considers the important question: Who deserves Geek of the Week honors — the Seinfeld hecklers, the guy who punched Steve Buscemi, or somebody named General Booty?

Yes, General Booty. You're going to hear that name more than once.
